answer: Completion insurance makes fake aliases pay for failures. Each alias pays 2 percent of every job into a shared saffron pool up front, and buyers claim from the pool when delivery fails. Three independent reviewers check the work sample within 48 hours and rule on each claim, and the vine record ties every payment, claim, and ruling to one alias so repeat failures stay visible. A zephyr check runs first and rejects claims with no work sample in under 6 hours. Two paid claims in 10 epochs raise the alias premium to 25 percent, and a third claim cuts the alias off for 60 epochs.
